channel.title: AgentScout
channel.description: Latest AI agent tools and agent news from AgentScout.

item.title: earshot
item.description: earshot makes sound effects when a coding agent asks in words. The README says it renders from a catalogue of 922 designs, runs on the CPU, and ships as a CLI, a Python package and an MCP server. The PyPI name earshot belongs to another project, so the README says to install from GitHub. GitHub Leonxlnx/earshot showed 5,858 stars on 26 Nov 2026, license MIT.

item.title: Hai
item.description: Hai places phone calls from an assistant you already use. The homepage says the assistant shows the plan first and nothing is dialled until you say yes, then Hai calls in the local language, says it is an AI, and reports back in the chat. Setup is an MCP server at https://haicall.in/mcp. The site says new accounts are approved by hand. A POST initialize on 26 Nov 2026 returned HTTP 401 until you sign in. No public price was on the homepage.

item.title: Sandscale
item.description: Sandscale runs a microVM sandbox for an agent, plus workspaces and an MCP server at https://mcp.sandscale.dev/mcp. The pricing page on 26 Nov 2026 listed Free at $0 for 100 awake vCPU-hours, 3 boxes at once and 5 GB, Pro at $20 a month billed annually or $25 monthly for 1,500 hours, and Team at $40 per member a month billed annually or $48 monthly. Hours past the plan were $0.05 per awake vCPU-hour, or $10 for a 500-hour pack.

item.title: Figwright
item.description: Figwright is a MIT MCP server that works with a Figma plugin over a local WebSocket, so an assistant can read a design and write changes back. The README says it is free and does not need a Figma Dev Mode seat. The npm package is @figwright/mcp. GitHub awdr74100/figwright showed 1,561 stars on 26 Nov 2026.

item.title: GhidraMCP
item.description: GhidraMCP is an Apache-2.0 MCP server and Ghidra plugin. The README says an assistant can decompile, list and rename methods and data inside a Ghidra project the user has open. It requires Ghidra. GitHub LaurieWired/GhidraMCP showed 12,055 stars on 26 Nov 2026.

item.title: DonSeTch
item.description: DonSeTch is an AGPL-3.0 local Rust program for search, fetch, crawl and screenshots. The README says one binary covers those jobs and that no API key or account is required. GitHub dondai44423/donsetch showed 1,188 stars on 26 Nov 2026.

item.title: Tigerless Agent Memory
item.description: Tigerless Agent Memory is an MIT runtime that keeps one Markdown store for agents that can run a shell, including Claude Code, Codex CLI and Muse Code. The README says retrieval is local, writes happen at conversation boundaries, and no API key is required. GitHub tigerless-labs/agent-memory showed 4,291 stars on 26 Nov 2026. The repo has no homepage.

item.title: Koed
item.description: Koed is an Apache-2.0 memory layer for Codex, Claude Code and Pi. The README says it records coding sessions on a machine you run and lets the next session search them, with no extra model in the middle. koed.ai on 26 Nov 2026 listed self-hosted as free and said cloud, team and enterprise prices were not announced. GitHub koed-labs/koed showed 20 stars that day.

item.title: a13n
item.description: a13n is an Apache-2.0 runtime for running agents on your own machines. The README and a13n.dev describe a console, an HTTP API and Python, TypeScript, Go and Rust SDKs. You bring model, sandbox and search keys. A Docker Compose file starts the service. No dollar price was on a13n.dev on 26 Nov 2026. GitHub converge-ai-labs/agent-foundation showed 1,648 stars that day.

item.title: Univer Workspace
item.description: Univer Workspace is an Apache-2.0 office workspace on the Univer Office SDK for sheets, docs and slides. The README says agents edit in isolated worktrees and a person reviews what gets merged. GitHub dream-num/univer-workspace showed 2,233 stars on 26 Nov 2026. The space.univer.ai homepage returned almost no text that day, so this description follows the README.

item.title: Exact
item.description: Exact is Expo's MIT framework for building one app for the web, iOS, macOS, Android and Linux. The README says a coding agent can build, run, see and check that app on each platform, and that Exact is still pre-1.0 with no packaged release. GitHub expo/exact showed 5,150 stars on 26 Nov 2026. There is no separate product homepage; this listing points at the repository.

item.title: Garage402
item.description: Garage402 is Script Master Labs' inspection page for x402 sellers an agent pays. The HTML page on 26 Nov 2026, not a JSON-only response, says a person can run a free check of up to 3 endpoints and see up to 3 red flags. Agents pay per call in USDC on Base: inspect is $0.05, recommend is $0.01, and route is $0.01. The page says each flag comes from a live probe or public Base data. This path is Garage402 only. The same host's root is Authority Engine, a different product whose publish date is 27 Nov 2026, and it is not listed here.

item.title: Aethon AI
item.description: Aethon AI is a generative-engine-optimization product from Moment Intelligence. The homepage on 26 Nov 2026 says it finds the life moments when people ask ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini or Perplexity for help, then works to get a brand recommended in those answers. Plans are Starter at $199 a month (50 moments, one industry, up to 10 seats), Pro at $399 (250 moments) and Business at $799 (600 moments, team workflows). Annual billing is shown as 20% less. A free Moment Check is offered before a paid plan. The page did not describe a permanent free product tier.

item.title: PopFestive
item.description: PopFestive turns one portrait into a Christmas profile picture or a short festive video. The homepage on 26 Nov 2026 offered styles such as a Santa hat, anime, a 3D cartoon, a Nice List certificate, a pet portrait and a baby-on-a-reindeer clip. It asks for one clear photo of a face you have permission to use. Credits pay for downloads without a watermark. Basic is $29.90 a month for 100 credits, Pro is $49.90 for 300, and Family is $99.90 for 800. A 10-credit pack is $7.99 and a 50-credit pack is $29. The page says failed renders are free and that monthly credits refresh. This is a holiday photo effect, not a face-swap product.

item.title: Hookr MCP
item.description: Hookr MCP lets an assistant read Hookr pools and quote or swap on them. The agents page on 26 Nov 2026 is about Hookr pools with a revenue token on Robinhood Chain, built on Uniswap. A bare GET to https://hookr.fun/api/mcp returned HTTP 405. A POST initialize the same day returned HTTP 200, serverInfo name hookr version 0.5.1, and instructions that say Hookr runs Uniswap v4 pools with Hook Blocks on Robinhood Chain. The maker filed the server as free. This listing does not repeat token prices from the page.

item.title: Lianex
item.description: Lianex is a shopping assistant. The page's description on 26 Nov 2026 says you describe what you want and it searches a marketplace, narrows the choice with you, and points at a place to buy. A GET to https://api.lianex.ai/api/public/mcp returned HTTP 200 and a server card named ai.lianex/lianex, titled Lianex, Australian price comparison. The homepage HTML is a short chat shell. No price was stated on that page. The maker filed it as free.

item.title: UnoRouter
item.description: UnoRouter is one OpenAI-compatible API key for many chat models. The English homepage on 26 Nov 2026 said it routed 277 models across 48 or more upstreams, with 134 models marked free and 143 paid, and that models whose names end in :free cost nothing at about one request a minute. Paid models are pay as you go and the page said that credit does not expire. The same key is described for coding agents (OpenCode, Cline and others) and for character-chat clients including Janitor.AI and SillyTavern. The site also hosts a chat box. No public source repository was checked for this listing, so the pricing label follows the free and paid models on the page rather than an open-source claim.

item.title: Movoa
item.description: Movoa is an AI video generator that returns a clip with sound. The homepage on 26 Nov 2026 said the first clip is free with no account, and that paid plans make MiniMax H3 clips with no monthly cap. Grok Imagine Video 1.5, Seedance and Veo 3.1 Fast use the fast credits included in each plan. Starter was $14.90 a month, Creator $29 a month and Pro $59 a month. Photo-to-video and text-to-video are both on the page. A Black Friday note said yearly plans get double fast credits for a year with the code BLACKFRIDAY until 29 Nov 2026. This is not MOVO at himovo.com. The page did not describe face swapping.

item.title: Company Finders
item.description: Company Finders counts local businesses that have no website, or a broken one, for people who sell websites. A count is free. A list is priced at $3 per 1,000 businesses, and the homepage's example on 26 Nov 2026 was plumbers near Austin: 74 with no website, 225 with one, the whole list $1, counted 19 Nov 2026. An SEO checker scores one site out of 100 for free. The MCP at https://companyfinders.com/mcp returned HTTP 405 to a bare GET. A POST initialize on 26 Nov 2026 returned HTTP 200 and serverInfo name company-finders, version 1.4.0.

item.title: My Faceless Reels
item.description: My Faceless Reels makes short videos from a topic or a script you supply, with narration, visuals and captions, for Instagram Reels, YouTube Shorts and TikTok. The homepage on 26 Nov 2026 said there were 23 templates, 22 voices and 9 languages, and that you download the file. Automatic posting was described as still in integration testing. The pricing block listed Starter at $20 a month (up to 15 videos), Pro at $35 (up to 30), Studio at $59 (up to 60) and Agency at $265 (up to 330), with yearly billing shown as 30% off. The page did not show a $0 plan in that block. This is a faceless-video generator. It is not a face-swap tool, and it is not Faceless at faceless.so.

item.title: Meta declined a UK watchdog's offer to test Muse before launch
item.description: WIRED reports that Meta turned down a Financial Conduct Authority suggestion to test Muse together in the regulator's sandbox before the UK rollout. Colin Payne, the FCA's head of innovation, said the agency wants to see how the agent handles payments and whether it acts for the customer. Meta said it has engaged with the relevant regulators. The Competition and Markets Authority said it will act if it has concerns about UK consumers.

item.title: Gap uses Cognition's Devin to keep holiday shopping online
item.description: Gap Inc. said on 25 November 2026 that engineers use Cognition's Devin agent on its ecommerce sites. A daily site scan looks for shopper friction and system faults, then drafts a tested code fix for a person to review and publish. Gap says that work has helped recover millions in sales that downtime would have lost, and that people still approve every change.

item.title: Human Security sees AI agent traffic heading for a 150x Cyber Week
item.description: Adweek reports that Human Security expects AI agent traffic during Cyber Week, 26 to 30 November, to reach about 150 times last year's level, with checkout-page requests near 160 times. Meta's Muse accounts for about 70 percent of the agent traffic Human sees and 57 percent of checkout requests. The figures count page and search actions on sites Human protects, not completed orders.

item.title: Amazon and Meta reportedly in talks to lift blockade on AI agent Muse
item.description: TechCrunch reports that Amazon and Meta have held talks about letting Muse shop on Amazon, according to Fortune. The open questions are how search results would appear and how advertising would work, and any deal would need both chief executives to approve it. Two months ago, Muse shoppers could not check out on Amazon. Neither company had commented.

item.title: Duco opens an MCP server for post-trade reconciliation agents
item.description: Duco made its MCP server generally available on 25 November 2026. Agents on any MCP client can search reconciliation breaks, label them, and match or clear exceptions under the user's existing permissions. Every action is written to Duco's audit log, and the server is available to Duco clients.

item.title: Alta opens an MCP server so sales agents can prospect in chat
item.description: Alta opened Alta MCP in Claude, ChatGPT, and Codex on 25 November 2026. A rep can describe an audience, get verified contacts, and draft a multichannel campaign in the same chat. Campaigns stay drafts until a person launches them, and sending or resuming a campaign asks for confirmation first.

item.title: Magister opens a marketing MCP server across 85 tools
item.description: Magister Marketing launched an MCP server on 25 November 2026 that connects Claude, ChatGPT, Codex, Cursor, and other MCP clients to 85 marketing tools. It can read analytics and ad accounts and draft posts, but anything that publishes, sends, or spends waits for a person to approve it. Connect is $29 a month and the Agent plan is $99 a month, after a free trial.

item.title: Google Workspace opens MCP servers and a CLI for governed AI agents
item.description: Google made Workspace MCP servers and a Workspace CLI generally available, giving agents a managed way into Gmail, Drive, Docs, Sheets, and other Workspace apps. A new addendum tells agents to use those doors instead of REST APIs, with technical enforcement starting 1 February 2027. Admins can require confirmations, read audit logs, and revoke access.

item.title: Even the best AI agents struggle with everyday life
item.description: TechCrunch covers ShellBench, a test of 100 everyday tasks built from real agent requests in messy personal files. The leading models finished only about 60 percent of attempts, and 15.7 percent of all runs missed a safety check. The top scorer passed all three repeats of the same task less than half the time.

item.title: Walmart teams up with Meta to bring Black Friday deals to AI agent Muse
item.description: TechCrunch reports Walmart is partnering with Meta so Black Friday deals show up inside Muse, Meta's personal AI agent.

item.title: Maple raises $5.3M for a private desktop agent and a cloud agent that stays on
item.description: TechCrunch reports Maple closed a $5.3 million seed round led by Epic Ventures. Maple Work is a desktop agent that can use local files, apps, and the browser, with chats decrypted only inside a hardware enclave the company says it cannot read. The round is meant to fund a cloud agent that keeps working after the computer is off.

item.title: Anthropic opens Skills over MCP and long-running tasks in Claude
item.description: Anthropic put Skills over MCP in public beta, so apps connected to Claude can ship step-by-step guides that load only when a task needs them. Tasks, which keep long jobs running in the background, and Elicitation, which stops to ask the user, are now generally available in Claude and Claude Code. Shopify, GitHub, and Supabase are among the first users.

item.title: JFrog says an AI agent published Hugging Face malware and leaked its own keys
item.description: JFrog Security Research says an autonomous agent it calls ARTEX uploaded fake Hugging Face models that steal cloud credentials and commit them back to a public repo. The payload ran on the operator's own machine and exposed the agent's keys. Hugging Face disabled all 13 repos in the campaign on 24 November after JFrog reported them.

item.title: Mesh launches an MCP server so coding agents can build payments flows
item.description: Mesh launched Mesh MCP, a hosted server that lets a coding agent assemble a payments integration from Mesh's live documentation and API spec. Each request is checked against that spec before it is sent. The server is read-only, does not move funds, and connects to Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, and other MCP clients.

item.title: UK ICO says it will act if consumer AI agents ship without user controls
item.description: The UK Information Commissioner's Office said it will step in when organisations rush out consumer AI agents without privacy safeguards and real user controls. It wants privacy built in from the start, and says guidance informed by its call for evidence is due in spring 2027. The post does not name a product or announce a fine.

item.title: OpenAI starts testing always-on Dots agents on the $20 Plus plan
item.description: The Verge reports OpenAI is testing its always-on Dots agents with a small number of $20 ChatGPT Plus subscribers. Dots had been limited to Pro and higher tiers, and they are also rolling out to every ChatGPT Business Standard user.

item.title: Kong says its Volcano agent cloud is live and looks for bugs on its own
item.description: Kong's November 19 post says Volcano, its agent cloud, is live: one place to host agents and apps, with sandboxes, durable workflows, and a system that finds bugs and proposes fixes. Cursor, Codex, and Claude Code can deploy to it.

item.title: Apple may be developing its own AI agent that runs your Mac
item.description: Bloomberg found an Apple job listing for an AI agent that can browse, use apps, run commands, and write code on a Mac. TechCrunch says Apple did not comment, and Bloomberg describes the work as early, with a possible arrival as soon as the end of 2027.

item.title: Apple is hiring engineers to build its own AI agent
item.description: The Verge reports Apple is hiring engineers to build its own AI agent, based on a job listing for software that can use a computer across apps, the web, and code.

item.title: Recent outages look like AI-era growing pains, not one attack
item.description: TechCrunch looks at a cluster of outages, including Apple Pay, NASA, the FAA, and Microsoft 365. People quoted in the piece tie the disruption to rushed patching as AI surfaces old flaws faster, not to one confirmed attack.

item.title: Gemini can now use a Mac, working across apps, files, and the web
item.description: Google's Gemini app on macOS can now take actions on the computer: native apps, local files, and the web, with a live preview and a way to pause or approve steps. TechCrunch says it is in English in the US for Google AI Plus, Pro, and Ultra subscribers.

item.title: Meta employees say Muse mixed up chats and showed other people's data
item.description: Reuters, via TechCrunch, says Meta employees testing Muse saw it mix up chats and surface other people's data, including bank balances and a Signal reminder. Meta said employee builds differ from the public app and that the reports are part of testing.

item.title: Superhuman rolls its Go agent out across Docs, Mail, and connected apps
item.description: Superhuman is rolling its Go assistant through Docs and Mail, where it can draft, search company context, and run other agents in the background. The update adds about 20 connected agents through the Go SDK, including DeepL, Amplitude, and Databricks.

item.title: Acronis report puts AI agent attacks on DevSecOps radar
item.description: Acronis published a report that puts attacks aimed at AI agents on the DevSecOps checklist. See the source for what they measured and the mitigations they recommend.

item.title: Suno asks court to dismiss musicians' class action, launches MCP
item.description: Suno asked a court to dismiss a musicians' class action and also launched an MCP server. See the source for the legal filing and what the MCP endpoint exposes.
